headline: Nvidia's board reportedly prepared to fire Jensen Huang over a second alleged affair as Trump ordered a new crackdown on chip diversion to China, while UNIDIR launched a Counter-IED knowledge-sharing compendium and a startup pitched AI to fight AI-engineered bioweapons.

points.text: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang after the New York Times reported a second alleged extramarital affair, this time with a senior executive who reports to him.

President Trump authorized a new crackdown, the third this year, on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, after Treasury Secretary Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Lutnick over a failure to flag an Nvidia customer as a national-security risk.
CSET warned of the risks of strategic overreaction to the Nvidia espionage allegations, as a separate analysis argued the scandal highlights contradictions at the heart of Trump's China policy.
UNIDIR launched a Counter-IED Compendium to strengthen global knowledge-sharing on preventing, mitigating, and countering improvised explosive devices.
A startup called Radical Numerics said it has built a model that can identify natural and AI-engineered pathogens without an internet connection, aiming to fight AI-enabled bioweapons with AI.
Transformer found that Hugging Face is still hosting a number of AI models marketed for cyberattacks, despite removing one.
The ITU's AI for Good discussed standards, safeguards, and cooperation for open-source AI.
